text:
Garry Kasparov is a Russian-born chess grandmaster and former world champion, known for his dynamic, aggressive playing style and extensive contributions to opening theory. Born Garik Kimovich Weinstein in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR (now Azerbaijan), he adopted his mother's surname Kasparov at age 12. He began studying chess at a young age, winning the Soviet Junior Championship in 1976 and rising rapidly through the ranks, becoming the youngest-ever world No. 1 in 1984 at age 22. He won the world championship five times against Anatoly Karpov, with a record of 21 wins, 19 losses, and 104 draws in 144 games. His rivalry with Karpov, often called the "two Ks," is one of the most significant in chess history.
Kasparov broke with FIDE in 1993, forming the Professional Chess Association (PCA) to challenge FIDE's authority, leading to a split in the world championship title. He won the PCA title and remained the top-rated player in the world until his retirement in 2005, holding a rating of 2812. After retiring from competitive chess, he remained active in chess through rapid and blitz exhibitions, coaching Magnus Carlsen, and promoting chess in education. He launched Kasparov Chess, a subscription-based online community, and supported various chess initiatives globally.
Beyond chess, Kasparov is a prominent political figure, having founded the United Civil Front to oppose Russian authoritarianism. He has been vocal in criticizing Vladimir Putin, supporting democratic reforms, and advocating for human rights. He has faced numerous political challenges, including arrests and harassment, and has been a key figure in anti-Putin movements, including the "Putin Must Go" campaign. Kasparov has also been recognized for his contributions to artificial intelligence, where he advocated for human-machine collaboration and the ethical use of AI.
Kasparov has authored numerous books, including the "My Great Predecessors" series and "Winter Is Coming," which critiques Putin's policies and calls for a global response to authoritarianism. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest chess players of all time, with a legacy that extends into politics, education, and public intellectualism.
